title: Finite Postnikov propagation of invertibility
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] with derived category $D(\mathcal A)$ and cohomology functors $H^q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and let $\mathcal T$ be a triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Let $\Phi,\Psi:D^+(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal T$ be exact triangulated functors on the full bounded-below derived category [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories], with specified shift isomorphisms $\xi_M:\Phi(M[1])\cong\Phi(M)[1]$ and $\zeta_M:\Psi(M[1])\cong\Psi(M)[1]$. Let $\eta:\Phi\to\Psi$ be a natural transformation satisfying $\zeta_M\eta_{M[1]}=\eta_M[1]\xi_M$. For $E\in D^+(\mathcal A)$ let $a,b\in\mathbf Z$ satisfy $a-1\le b$ and $H^q(E)=0$ for $q<a$. Suppose $\eta_{H^q(E)[0]}$ is invertible for every $a\le q\le b$, where $H^q(E)[0]$ denotes the cohomology object placed in degree zero. Then $\eta_{\tau_{\le b}E}$ is invertible, with canonical upper truncation from [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. This includes the empty interval $b=a-1$.

source.place: Tag 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle): the successive cohomology triangles; finite induction and natural-transformation argument supplied in report.md

proof.text: Put $E_q=\tau_{\le q}E$ for every integer $q\ge a-1$. The truncation-cohomology statement gives $H^i(E_q)\cong H^i(E)$ for $i\le q$ and $H^i(E_q)=0$ for $i>q$. Thus $H^i(E_q)=0$ for $i<a$ as well, and $E_q$ is in $D^+(\mathcal A)$. Each $C_q=H^q(E)[0][-q]$ is also bounded below, being concentrated in degree $q$. The full bounded-below subcategory has the inherited triangulated structure, so a distinguished triangle of these objects in $D(\mathcal A)$ is a distinguished triangle in the domain of $\Phi,\Psi$. We will prove $P(q)$: $\eta_{E_q}$ is invertible, for $a-1\le q\le b$.

source.place: Tag 05RU (definition-unbounded-derived-category): the full triangulated subcategory D+; Tag 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle); truncation cohomology in homology.tex Tag 0118 (section-truncations)

proof.text: For $q=a-1$, every cohomology object of $E_{a-1}$ is zero by step 1: in degrees at most $a-1$ this is the lower-bound hypothesis, and in larger degrees it is upper truncation. The map $E_{a-1}\to0$ induces isomorphisms on all cohomology objects, hence is an isomorphism by cohomology detection in $D^+(\mathcal A)$. In particular $\mathrm{id}_{E_{a-1}}=0$. The functors are additive by the definition of exact triangulated functor, so $\mathrm{id}_{\Phi(E_{a-1})}=\Phi(\mathrm{id}_{E_{a-1}})=\Phi(0)=0$, and likewise for $\Psi$. The zero map $\Psi(E_{a-1})\to\Phi(E_{a-1})$ is therefore a two-sided inverse of $\eta_{E_{a-1}}$: both composites are the zero identities. This proves $P(a-1)$.

source.place: Tag 05RU (definition-unbounded-derived-category) and Tag 05RT (lemma-acyclic): acyclic objects become zero; the zero-object argument for additive functors is written out here

proof.text: The assumed shift equation rewrites as $\eta_{M[1]}=\zeta_M^{-1}\circ\eta_M[1]\circ\xi_M$. Thus $\eta_{M[1]}$ is invertible exactly when $\eta_M$ is: the shift is an autoequivalence, so its inverse shift carries an inverse of $\eta_M[1]$ back to an inverse of $\eta_M$. Iterating this equivalence forwards, and backwards by applying it to $M[-1]$, proves invertibility on every integral shift of $M$. Canonical identifications of iterated shifts cause no difficulty: for any isomorphism $u:M\to N$, naturality gives $\eta_N=\Psi(u)\circ\eta_M\circ\Phi(u)^{-1}$. Consequently the hypothesis on $\eta_{H^q(E)[0]}$ implies that $\eta_{C_q}$ is invertible for every $a\le q\le b$.

source.place: Tags 0145 and 014V (definition-triangulated and definition-exact-functor-triangulated-categories): shifts and their inverses; the displayed conjugation and its iteration use the hypotheses directly

proof.text: Fix $q$ with $a\le q\le b$ and assume $P(q-1)$. The successive-truncation triangle gives the distinguished triangle $E_{q-1}\longrightarrow E_q\longrightarrow C_q\longrightarrow E_{q-1}[1]$. Its three vertices belong to $D^+(\mathcal A)$ by step 1. Apply the two-out-of-three theorem for a shift-compatible natural transformation between exact triangulated functors, with $\alpha=\eta$, $X=E_{q-1}$, $Y=E_q$, $Z=C_q$, and the specified comparisons $\xi,\zeta$. Its compatibility condition is exactly the equation in the statement of this item. The first component is invertible by the induction hypothesis and the third by step 3, so its middle component $\eta_{E_q}$ is invertible. This proves $P(q-1)\Rightarrow P(q)$.

source.place: Tag 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle), successive upper-truncation triangle with index q-1; Tag 014A (lemma-third-isomorphism-triangle) via the cited shift-compatible natural-transformation theorem

proof.text: The integer $N=b-a+1$ is nonnegative. Starting with $P(a-1)$ from step 2 and using step 4 exactly $N$ times proves $P(b)$, which is the required invertibility of $\eta_{\tau_{\le b}E}$. When $N=0$, equivalently $b=a-1$, the conclusion is already step 2 and no assumption on a cohomology component is used.
